name: Double Ratio Backspread
summary: A call backspread (sell 1 nearer strike, buy 2 further strikes) plus a put backspread in the same expiry - four leg-lines, defined risk, strongly long volatility with convex payoffs in both tails.

legs.strike_rule: 0.30-0.35 delta put (nearer the money, above the long puts)
0.30-0.35 delta call (nearer the money, below the long calls)

max_profit: UNLIMITED on the upside (2 long calls net), and (put strikes x 100) minus cost on the downside - the payoff is convex in both tails
max_loss: at the long strikes at expiry: on each side, (short strike - long strike) x 100 x 1 contract, plus or minus the net premium. Compute the exact worst case numerically across a spot grid at entry; it is bounded.
breakevens: four breakevens (two per side) - compute numerically at entry and store them

greeks.gamma: positive in both tails, negative at the long strikes

when_to_use: IV rank <= 20 with steep skew (so the nearer short strikes pay well relative to the further longs) and an expectation of a large move. It is the structure to use when you want long-vol convexity without paying a straight strangle's premium.
entry_rules: Net premium: target a credit or a debit no larger than 15% of the maximum modeled loss
Ratio exactly 2 long : 1 short per side, with the shorts CLOSER to the money than the longs (this is what makes it defined risk)
Worst-case modeled loss (evaluated at each long strike at expiry) <= 2% of equity
DTE 30-60 so the position has time to move; exit before 21 DTE
OI >= 500 on all strikes, spread <= 10% of mid
Alpaca level 3: each short is covered by a long at a strike that bounds it. Validate leg-by-leg before submit; if the broker flags any short as uncovered it becomes level 4.
Alpaca mleg supports up to 4 legs - this structure is exactly 4 leg-lines with ratios 2/1/1/2
management_rules: Take profit at 100% of the modeled maximum loss (i.e. when the gain equals the worst-case risk)
Hard time stop: close at 21 DTE - the maximum-loss zone sits exactly at the long strikes at expiry, which is where the position drifts
Loss stop: close at 60% of the modeled max loss
Volatility exit: if IV rank rises above 45 and the position is green, close
If spot sits within 2% of either long strike with < 30 DTE remaining, close - that is the pain point
exit_rules: Force-close by 15:45 ET on expiration day, always
Close immediately if either short leg's extrinsic < $0.10 or |delta| >= 0.85
Ex-dividend guard on the short call
Never let expiration resolve the ratio: a pinned long strike at expiry produces the worst outcome and an assignment on the short
assignment_risk: One short call and one short put per unit. Both are closer to the money than the longs, so they go ITM first - the assignment guard fires regularly on this structure. Treat it as high-maintenance.
buying_power: Broker-computed maximum modeled loss, roughly (short strike - long strike) x 100 per side net of premium.
liquidity_needs: OI >= 500 on all four strikes; the 2x long legs must be closeable in size.
common_mistakes: Building it with the shorts FURTHER from the money (that is a naked ratio spread, level 4, unlimited risk); entering in high IV; holding into expiry where the long strikes are the maximum-pain points.
zero_dte_notes: Not recommended: the structure needs a large move over time, and 0DTE decay at the long strikes is punishing. If tested intraday, use a 60-minute time stop and close by 15:30 ET.
family: four-leg structures (iron condors, iron butterflies, condors, double calendars/diagonals, boxes, jelly rolls, conversions/reversals, double verticals, double ratio spreads)
